source_user: Advanced cluster case RoCE-34: Diagnose a RoCE-based GPU cluster whose collective communication has unstable tail latency. Variant 34 must state assumptions, define a falsifiable hypothesis, name metrics, and include one failure or rollback condition.
source_assistant: An expert answer should distinguish model-domain mechanisms from runtime measurements. Required technical anchors: check lossless-priority configuration, PFC/ECN, MTU, route symmetry, congestion, NIC counters, queue pairs, and whether a fallback path is hiding the real fault. It must report topology, workload, units, baselines, confounders, and evidence needed before claiming improvement.
corrected_answer: Treat this as provisional RoCE GPU-cluster cluster_performance guidance for 34. Assume a multi-node collective workload, but do not assume lossless behavior, GPU-direct transfers, symmetric routes, or absence of a fallback transport. Separate measured facts, estimates, and unknowns; record GPU/NIC/switch topology, PCIe/NVLink affinity, firmware/driver/library versions, MTU, link speed, VLAN/priority mapping, queue-pair and message-size/concurrency distributions, clock alignment, and the selected transport. Trace the path from the collective call through verbs work requests/completions and registered host/GPU buffers to NIC, fabric, and peer, and correlate application timestamps with NIC and switch counters. Use a controlled measurement and causal-attribution plan. First capture immutable baselines and configuration snapshots; avoid exposing credentials or unrestricted destructive commands. Falsifiable hypothesis: the unstable tail is caused by a path/configuration mismatch or congestion event rather than an unmeasured workload change. Interleave matched baseline and treatment runs with fixed placement, software, warm-up, message mix, concurrency, and sample count. Report p50/p95/p99 latency in ms or us, throughput, step-time p99, timeout/retry/error rate, drops, ECN marks, PFC pause duration, retransmissions, queue/completion errors, GPU utilization, and confidence intervals or bootstrap uncertainty. Localize by comparing per-rank and per-hop data, checking MTU and route symmetry, priority/PFC/ECN behavior, queue-pair pressure, and whether host staging or fallback changes the path; do not infer causality from one counter. Apply one reversible canary at a time and define a rollback if correctness checks fail, timeout/error rate rises, p99 worsens, drops or pauses increase, or the improvement is not reproducible. Stop on packet loss, link flaps, data-integrity mismatch, or safety-policy violations, and preserve timestamps and command outputs for review.

quality_dimensions.requirement_coverage: covers assumptions, mechanism, boundary conditions, failure modes, measurement plan, and safety limits
quality_dimensions.technical_specificity: names RoCE, verbs/completions, topology, PFC/ECN, MTU, routing, queues, fallback, and path instrumentation
quality_dimensions.falsifiability: matched interleaved baseline, fixed confounders, metrics, uncertainty, and rollback thresholds
quality_dimensions.actionability: ordered evidence collection and reversible canary procedure

risks: platform-specific commands or counter semantics may differ
tail results can be confounded by workload drift, clock skew, or hidden fallback
PFC changes can amplify congestion and blast radius
evidence_required: topology and software inventory
transport-selection evidence and verbs completion/error logs
per-rank application latency distributions
NIC and switch counters correlated by synchronized timestamps
matched baseline/treatment results with sample counts and uncertainty
correctness, timeout, retry, drop, ECN, and PFC observations
